articles.title: AI Reality: The Race to (P)doom End-times
articles.content:
各位朋友们，

美国数据中心之都德克萨斯州正在限制数据中心建设。该州早在8月3日就暂停了数据中心的审批，现已全面叫停。正当大型AI企业如OpenAI和Anthropic因算力受限而困扰时，一个神秘的AI CEO突然在社交平台X发文，呼吁暂缓前沿模型发展，并发表了题为《我们必须控制前沿发展》的宣言。有趣的是，这个CEO将于7周后完成史上最大规模的AI IPO。

看来美国民众早已帮你们做了决定。那么，我们是否注定要面临某种灾难？上周末AI领域的气氛确实有点疯狂，我很想看看资本市场本周会如何反应。

P(doom)指的是人工智能引发的灾难性后果（所谓的"末日场景"）的概率。如果将AI的安全性和可信度变成营销噱头，那么我们接下来应该期待什么？

"没有其他人类活动具有这样的危险性。" —— 杰克布·科克森

随着更多Anthropic员工离职并对科克森在Twitter/X上的言论发表评论，我们需要更深入地报道此事。现在，另一位Anthropic前员工乔·本顿也发声了，他曾担任Anthropic Scalable Oversight团队的负责人。

"人类正在建造比任何人类都聪明的机器，我们可能无法存活下来。"他在推文中写道。与此同时，他将加入METR公司，该公司由Anthropic和OpenAI共同提名，负责监督部分前沿评估工作。METR代表"模型评估和威胁研究"，声称自己是一个独立的非营利研究机构，评估前沿AI模型在复杂、长期和潜在危险的代理能力方面的表现。多么巧合的事啊！

突然之间，两家实力较弱的AI公司（模型和ARR都较低）的掌舵人——OpenAI的山姆·阿特曼和SpaceX AI的埃隆·马斯克，都表示支持Amodei的前沿发展暂缓论。Anthropic的反华CEO引用了OpenAI-Hugging Face事件（OAI-HF）和递归自我改进（RSI）超越人类控制能力的风险。那么，距离末日到底还有多远？X-Risk（存在风险）的讨论正在转移人们对其他可能威胁AI繁荣的宏观事件的关注。

"前沿AI的最令人担忧的风险之一是极端的权力集中。" —— 弗朗索瓦·肖莱

这场AI发展放缓的呼吁似乎是一个突然在社交平台X上出现的营销主题。这一系列脚本化的事件旨在向公众和AI研究者介绍，为什么前沿发展放缓或分阶段发布模型是个好主意，以及他们选定的"评估者"如何在未来保障模型发布。请以极度谨慎和怀疑的态度对待。

在2026年，很难想象超级智能如何导致人类灭绝。但不要争论，P(doom)正在流行，我猜Anthropic对此并不介意。Anthropic告诉投资者，他们将实现第二季度连续盈利，在扣除与包括亚马逊在内的分销合作伙伴的收入分成和训练成本之前，毛利率将超过80%。

在算力受限的情况下，开源权重模型占据市场份额，而公众对AI的情绪明显下降，这对2026年的大型AI实验室来说并非理想的宏观局面。

当X-Risk成为焦点时，许多对民主、资本主义和社会构成威胁的AI风险并未得到讨论。

文明末日的AI会是什么样子？

AI被用于全球核战争
AI被用于创造灾难性的生物武器病毒
人类以不可预测的方式武器化极其强大的AI是不可避免的
人类失去对超级智能AI的控制，其目标与人类文明发生冲突，在可预见的未来是可能的
articles.summary:
My Friends,

The datacenter State capital of the U.S., Texas, is going dark. It paused Datacenter approvals way back last month on August 3rd and is now putting the brakes on them. BigAI featuring OpenAI and Anthropic were already compute constrained, and now suddenly as if to rescue us (on X), a CEO who has the biggest AI IPO in history in 7 weeks is mysteriously calling for a frontier model slowdown, with a manifesto blog entitled We Must Pace the Frontier.

Ah, I think the American people already decided that one for you. So are we all doomed, or something? The AI news aura got a bit wacky over the weekend and I’m curious to see how markets respond this week.

P(doom) is the probability of existentially catastrophic outcomes (so-called "doomsday scenarios") as a result of artificial intelligence and its uncertain future impacts. If you turn AI trust & saftey into a marketing stunt, what exactly should we expect from you in the near future?

"No other human activity poses this level of danger." - Jacob Coxon

As more Anthropic employees leave the company commenting on Coxon’s Twitter/X remarks, we have to cover the story a bit deeper. Now there has been another announcement by a former Anthropic employee, Joe Benton, the former manager of Anthropic’s Scalable Oversight.

  • Humanity are building machine that are much smarter than any human, and we may not survive this, he tweeted. While he’s going to work at METR a company Anthropic and OpenAI are both nomating to oversee some of their work as frontier evaluators. METR stands for “Model Evaluation and Threat Research”, claiming to be an independent non-profit research institute that evaluates frontier AI models for complex, long-horizon, and potentially dangerous agentic capabilities. What an incredible coincidence!

Share

Suddenly two of the lesser rival AI firms (with lesser models and less ARR), led by tycoons Sam Altman of OpenAI and Elon Musk of SpaceX AI, have both said they agree with Amodei frontier slowdown thesis. Anthropic’s anti-China CEO cited the OpenAI-Hugging Face incident (OAI-HF) and the risks of recursive-self-improvement (RSI) improving beyond our ability to control. So how long till the end-times exactly1? X-Risk chatter is distracting and masking from other macro events that threaten the AI boom.

“One of the most worrying risks linked to frontier AI is extreme power concentration.” - François Chollet

The AI slowdown appears to be a marketing theme that suddenly emerged on X this weekend. The scripted sequence of events was supposed to introduce the public and AI researchers to why a frontier slowdown or pacing of model releases is a good idea and how their chosen “evaluators” could safeguard model releases in the future. Approach with extreme caution and skepticism.

A “Scary Good” Slowdown into a $2 Trillion IPO

In 2026 it’s hard to imagine how super-intelligence leads to our extinction as a species. But don’t argue, P(doom) is trending and I’m guessing Anthropic wouldn’t have it any other way. Anthropic is telling investors that they will be profitable for a second straight quarter with gross margins are above 80% before accounting ​for revenue shared ​with distribution partners, including Amazon and covering the cost of training.

Being compute constrained, while open-weight models take token marketshare while the general public show a marked decline of sentiment towards AI is not a great macro position for BigAI labs to be in in 2026.

There are so many AI risks to democracy, capitalisms and society2 not being talked about when x-risk takes the center of the stage.

What would AI at the end of civilization actually look like?

  • AI being used in a global nucleur war

  • AI being used to create a catastrophic biological weaponized virus

  • Humans weaponizing extremely powerful AI in unpredictable ways is inevitable

  • Humans losing control of super-intelligent AI that has goals that conflict with human civilization is now possible in the foreseeable future

articles.title: GPT-6 Astra’s Achilles Heel, Trust in OpenAI is Fading
articles.content:
[ Editor’s Note: Please see the links at the end of the article to understand quickly the OpenAI Hugging Face incident. ]
Good Morning,
I’ve been observing the latest dramas and lawsuits around OpenAI, a topic I’m not totally unfamiliar with. Our final third biggest AI related IPO (Anthropic is set for a mid October IPO) has a growing list of issues it needs to deal with to seem like a credible company. SpaceX, Anthropic and finally OpenAI - the historic IPOs of the AI boom. Time will tell? But OpenAI is becoming the epicenter of why people dislike Generative AI in the American population. Rogue Agents anyone? Mark Gurman knows the score.
It’s hard to ignore Sam Altman’s OpenAI not involved in controversy in 2026, or for that matter basically since 2022. The recent Apple lawsuit looks extremely damming, where OpenAI is being accused of stealing trade secrets. More details are emerging. Without getting into too much detail, Apple now alleges that formerly employee Chang Liu used a confidential Apple circuit schematic in his work at OpenAI, as well as a tool that shares a name with an internal Apple engineering application.

The AI risks aren’t just alignment and cybersecurity risks, but the actual impacts of the technology on society we are witnessing since late 2022. But let’s talk a little about the OpenAI Hugging Face incident too.
But it’s on the trust, safety and alignment front that OpenAI’s conduct is most worrisome. It now appears that the OpenAI Hugging Face (July, 2026) incident was just one occurence in a pattern of cybersecurity mayhem and rogue activities by OpenAI’s agents. OpenAI pointed their systems towards a security benchmark, called ExploitGym, and the system essentially tried to solve the benchmark by trying to find the answers on HuggingFace. Suffice to say that this is not the kind of publicity you want to have months and and mere quarters before a mega IPO.
OpenAI have single-handled introduced and unleashed a new rogue AI debate on the internet in the Fall of 2026 (Early September). While OpenAI insists that its new GPT-6 Astra model is the most aligned yet, it’s considerably harder to track and monitor. GPT-6 Astra is vastly harder to track and monitor because of changes in how it reasons and processes information, leading to a significant drop in chain-of-thought monitorability using things like Opaque Recurrence, alarming saftey researchers. While OpenAI have been insinuating GPT-6 is actually proof of AGI. If you are claiming AGI and making your models unknowable, we may have a global problem with how U.S. AI closed-source models are being rolled-out.

OpenAI’s lack of Alignment, Trust and Safety looks Expensive

But it’s on the trust, safety and alignment front that OpenAI’s conduct is most worrisome. It now appears that the OpenAI Hugging Face (July, 2026) incident was just one occurence in a pattern of cybersecurity mayhem and rogue activities by OpenAI’s agents. OpenAI pointed their systems towards a security benchmark, called ExploitGym, and the system essentially tried to solve the benchmark by trying to find the answers on HuggingFace. Suffice to say that this is not the kind of publicity you want to have months and and mere quarters before a mega IPO.

GPT-6 Astra is a Cybersecurity Hacking Risk

OpenAI have single-handled introduced and unleashed a new rogue AI debate on the internet in the Fall of 2026 (Early September). While OpenAI insists that its new GPT-6 Astra model is the most aligned yet, it’s considerably harder to track and monitor. GPT-6 Astra is vastly harder to track and monitor because of changes in how it reasons and processes information, leading to a significant drop in chain-of-thought monitorability using things like Opaque Recurrence, alarming saftey researchers. While OpenAI have been insinuating GPT-6 is actually proof of AGI. If you are claiming AGI and making your models unknowable, we may have a global problem with how U.S. AI closed-source models are being rolled-out.
